title: Science and Health
description: Ten short stories, columns, a diary entry and an e-mail about science and health: a research ship, a nurse's day, a flu shot clinic, sleep and the brain, a science fair, a pharmacist's advice, physical therapy, a tiger's checkup, chocolate and a translation team at a free clinic.

lessons.title: Notes from a Research Vessel
lessons.summary: A scientist spends 5 days on a research ship and finds that the shells of small sea creatures have grown thinner.
lessons.text:
My name is Laura Kim, and I am a scientist at a small ocean research lab. Last week, I spent 5 days on our research vessel. A research vessel is a ship that carries scientists and their equipment. Our vessel is not big, but it has a small lab, a kitchen and beds for 8 people.

Our team studies tiny sea creatures that live inside shells. They build their shells from materials in the water, and they are food for many bigger animals, including fish and whales.

Why are we interested in their shells? Every day, the ocean takes in a large amount of carbon from the air. When this carbon mixes with sea water, it forms a weak acid. The acid is not dangerous for people who swim in the sea, but it makes it harder for small creatures to build strong shells. In water with more acid, their shells can grow thin.

On the first day, 2 members of our team dived near some rocks to collect creatures from the sea floor. Diving is an important part of our work, because many creatures live where we cannot reach them from the vessel. While my colleagues were diving, I was collecting sand on a nearby beach. Small shells often get mixed with the sand, so a bag of sand can tell us a lot.

In the evening, we studied the shells in the vessel's lab. Some shells were thick and strong. Others were very thin. We measured each shell and wrote down the numbers.

Back on land, we compared our numbers with numbers from 10 years ago. The shells we found this year were significantly thinner than the old ones. The difference was even bigger near the places with the most acid in the water. There, the shells were significantly thinner than anywhere else.

Our conclusion was simple: more carbon in the air means more acid in the sea, and more acid means thinner shells. Of course, one study is not enough to reach a final conclusion, so we will repeat it next year. By then, we will have collected shells from 3 more beaches.

I wish we had started this study earlier. If we had collected sand and shells 30 years ago, we could have compared many more years. Still, I am happy with our work. Standing on the deck of the vessel on the last evening, I watched the sun go down and thought about the tiny creatures in the water below us.

Questions:
What is a research vessel?
It is a ship that carries scientists and their equipment.
What happens when carbon mixes with sea water?
It forms a weak acid.
Why is the acid a problem for small creatures?
It makes it harder for them to build strong shells, so their shells can grow thin.
What was Laura doing while her colleagues were diving?
She was collecting sand on a nearby beach.
What was the team's conclusion?
More carbon in the air means more acid in the sea, and more acid means thinner shells.
What does Laura wish?
She wishes they had started the study earlier.

lessons.title: A Nurse's Day
lessons.summary: A nurse writes in her diary about a long day at the hospital and an evening with a comedy on TV.
lessons.text:
Thursday, March 6

My shift at the hospital started at 7 this morning. I always go to work in jeans and change into my blue uniform at the hospital.

My first patient was Mr. Evans, an older man who had come in the night before. He was breathing heavily, and he said he had a sharp pain in his chest. A pain in the chest can be a symptom of many things, so the doctor ordered some tests. While we were waiting for the results, I sat with Mr. Evans and helped him take slow, deep breaths. "Take a slow breath in for 4 seconds, then let it out for 4 seconds," I told him. After a few minutes, his breath was calmer, and he was no longer breathing so heavily.

The tests showed that his heart was fine. Mr. Evans had been carrying heavy bags of soil in his garden for 3 days, and he must have hurt a muscle in his chest. The doctor explained that the pain was sharp because the muscle was tired, not because of his heart. "I should have asked my son to help me," Mr. Evans said with a smile.

Later, a young woman came in with a fever and a cough. Those are typical symptoms of a cold or the flu, so she wore a mask, and so did I. On our floor, patients with these symptoms always wear a mask, because a mask protects other patients.

The work on our floor is constant. There is a constant sound of phones and machines, and patients need constant care. Some days, I see a lot of suffering. However, I also see how much a kind word can do. A nurse cannot take away all suffering, but she can make it smaller. That is why I chose this job.

At 7 in the evening, I took off my uniform, put my jeans back on and drove home. I was too tired to read, so I watched a comedy on TV. It was a silly comedy about a family on vacation, and I laughed a lot. Laughing is my favorite way to relax after a long day.

Now it is almost midnight. I wish I had gone to bed earlier, but the comedy was too funny to stop.

Questions:
What does the nurse wear on her way to work?
She wears jeans and changes into her blue uniform at the hospital.
What symptoms did Mr. Evans have?
He was breathing heavily, and he had a sharp pain in his chest.
Why did Mr. Evans have a pain in his chest?
He had been carrying heavy bags of soil, and he must have hurt a muscle.
Why did the young woman wear a mask?
She had a fever and a cough, and a mask protects other patients.
Why did the nurse choose her job?
A nurse cannot take away all suffering, but she can make it smaller.
What did the nurse do after work?
She drove home and watched a comedy on TV.

lessons.title: Free Flu Shots for the Whole Family
lessons.summary: A town gives free flu shots in a school gym, and many families come, some children in costumes.
lessons.text:
Last Saturday, the town's health center gave free flu shots in the gym of Riverside School. The health center always tries to announce events like this early. "We announce our free shot days 2 weeks ahead, because we want families to plan," said Dr. Sam Ortiz, who runs the health center. "When we are announcing a shot day, we use the local paper, our website and the radio."

Doctors widely recommend a flu shot every year for everyone over 6 months old. "The flu changes a little every year, so last year's shot is not enough," Dr. Ortiz explained. "A shot gives your body a boost. It teaches your body to fight the flu before you catch it. The boost takes about 2 weeks to work, so October is a good time to get your shot."

More than 400 people came, from Riverside and from nearby towns. Many teens came with their parents, and some teens came on their own. "My friends and I play soccer, and we don't want to miss games because we're sick," said Kevin, 15. Like most teens, he was a little nervous about the shot, but he said it was over in a second.

Because it was the weekend before Halloween, many children came in costumes. A little girl was dressed as a princess, with a long pink dress. Her brother came as a ghost in a white sheet, and a 6-year-old boy came as a warrior with a paper shield. "Warriors are not afraid of shots," the warrior said, and he did not cry. The princess and the ghost did not cry either.

As a bonus, every child received a sticker and an apple. Adults got a bonus too: free coffee from a nearby bakery.

So many people came that the shot day needed an extension. It was supposed to end at 2, but the gym stayed open until 4. "We are happy we could give the day an extension," Dr. Ortiz said. "If we had closed at 2, about 100 people would have gone home without a shot."

Shots are also widely available at doctors' offices and drug stores. The health center is now announcing one more free shot day, which will be held at the public library on November 15. By the end of November, the center will have given free shots to more than 1,000 people.

Questions:
How does the health center announce its free shot days?
It announces them in the local paper, on its website and on the radio.
How does a flu shot give your body a boost?
It teaches your body to fight the flu before you catch it.
Why did Kevin get a flu shot?
He plays soccer and does not want to miss games because he is sick.
What costumes did some children wear?
A girl came as a princess, her brother came as a ghost, and a boy came as a warrior.
What bonus did the children receive?
Every child received a sticker and an apple.
Why did the shot day need an extension?
So many people came that the gym stayed open until 4 instead of 2.

lessons.title: What Your Brain Does at Night
lessons.summary: A short science column explains what happens in the brain during sleep and how to sleep better.
lessons.text:
THE SCIENCE CORNER: What Your Brain Does at Night

For most of human existence, people went to sleep soon after dark and woke up with the sun. Electric light is very new in the long story of human existence. Today we have lights, screens and busy lives, and many of us sleep less than we should. Surely you have noticed how hard everything feels after a short night. Scientists have learned a lot about why this happens.

Falling asleep is not like turning off a light. It is a slow transition. First, your body relaxes and your breath becomes slower. Then your brain passes through several stages, from light sleep to deep sleep and back again. One full cycle takes about 90 minutes, and most people go through 4 or 5 cycles every night. Toward morning, there is a transition to lighter sleep, and you dream more.

During sleep, your brain is busy. One of its most important jobs is the formation of memories. The things you learned during the day are sorted, and the important ones are stored. Memory formation is one reason why students who sleep well after studying usually remember more.

Sleep also helps to restore your body. While you sleep, your muscles repair themselves, and your brain clears away waste. A good night's sleep restores your energy and your mood. In contrast, after a bad night, people react more slowly and feel somewhat less patient. Surely nobody wants to feel like that every day.

What can you do to sleep better? Bright light in the morning helps to set your body's clock. In contrast, bright screens late in the evening can trigger the opposite effect and make it harder to fall asleep. Coffee late in the day can also trigger problems, because its effect lasts for many hours.

Some people have to reverse their normal day. Nurses and other night workers sleep during the day and work at night. When they reverse their day, they need dark rooms and quiet homes. Even then, they often sleep somewhat less than other people.

If you often lie awake for hours, or if you feel tired even after a full night, you might have a sleep disorder. A sleep disorder is a medical problem, and doctors can treat it. Many people wish they had talked to a doctor sooner, so don't wait. A few weeks of good sleep can restore more than you think.

Questions:
Why is falling asleep not like turning off a light?
It is a slow transition through several stages of sleep.
How long does one full cycle of sleep take?
It takes about 90 minutes.
Why does sleep matter for learning?
During sleep, the brain works on the formation of memories.
What can trigger problems with falling asleep?
Bright screens late in the evening and coffee late in the day can trigger problems.
Who has to reverse their normal day?
Nurses and other night workers have to reverse their normal day.
What should you do if you think you have a sleep disorder?
You should talk to a doctor, because doctors can treat it.

lessons.title: The Science Fair
lessons.summary: Ben builds a small electric railway for the school science fair, fixes a problem and wins a prize.
lessons.text:
Every spring, Lincoln Middle School holds a science fair, and this year Ben, who is 12, decided to build a small electric railway. For Ben, it was the most exciting project he had ever started.

He spent 3 weeks on it. First, he fixed 2 metal rails to a long wooden board with tiny screws. He used 40 screws in total, one every few inches. Then he built a simple circuit. The circuit connected a battery to the rails, so that electricity could flow through the rails to a small motor in the train. The train itself was made of plastic, and its wheels were metal, because plastic does not carry electricity.

Ben's question was simple: how does the angle of the railway change the speed of the train? He put books under one end of the board to make a hill. He tested 5 different angles, and he measured the speed at each angle 3 times. At a small angle, the train climbed the hill easily. At a large angle, it climbed very slowly, and at the largest angle, it stopped in the middle of the hill.

The night before the fair, the train suddenly stopped working. Ben looked at every part of the circuit and finally found the problem: one of the screws had come loose, so a rail was no longer connected. He tightened the screw, and the train ran again. If he hadn't checked the screws, he would have had no project at the fair.

At the fair, Ben's railway stood next to a project by a girl named Ella. She had made a water filter from plastic bottles, sand and stones. At first, her filter had a leak, and water ran across the table. Ella fixed the leak with tape, and her filter worked well. Ben helped her dry the table, and they both laughed about the leak.

At the end of the day, the judges declared the winners. Ella earned third place, and Ben earned second place. A girl who had built a solar oven was declared the winner. "Congratulations!" Ben's teacher said, shaking his hand. Ben said congratulations to Ella and to the winner, too. Getting a prize was exciting, but the most exciting moment was seeing his train climb the hill.

Questions:
What did Ben build for the science fair?
He built a small electric railway.
How did Ben fix the rails to the board?
He fixed them with tiny screws, one every few inches.
What did Ben want to find out?
He wanted to find out how the angle of the railway changes the speed of the train.
Why did the train stop working the night before the fair?
One of the screws had come loose, so a rail was no longer connected.
What was wrong with Ella's filter at first?
It had a leak, and water ran across the table.
What place did Ben earn?
He earned second place.

lessons.title: Advice from the Pharmacist
lessons.summary: Nora gets many bug bites while staying with her cousin, and a pharmacist gives her good advice.
lessons.text:
My name is Nora. Last July, I spent a week with my cousin Mia, who lives in a small town near a lake. On the second evening, we played in the garden until it was dark. There were lots of bushes around the garden, and we ran between the bushes and hid behind them. My cousin was wearing long pants, but I was wearing shorts.

I didn't notice anything that evening. However, the next morning, I had more than 20 red bug bites on my legs. The bites hurt a little, and I wanted to scratch them all the time. I had also ripped my favorite shorts on a bush.

My cousin's mother took us to the drug store in town. The pharmacist, Mr. Grant, looked at my legs. He acknowledged that the bites looked bad. "That is a lot of bites," he said. "But they are not serious. Bug bites are very common in summer, especially near water and bushes."

Mr. Grant gave me 3 recommendations. His first recommendation was a cream for the bites. It was a thick white cream, and he told me to put a thin layer on each bite 2 or 3 times a day. His second recommendation was to wash the bites with cool water and soap. His third recommendation was the hardest one: "Try not to scratch. If you scratch, the bites will take longer to heal."

He also made a suggestion for the rest of my visit. "My suggestion is simple," he said. "When you play near the bushes in the evening, wear long pants and long sleeves." He acknowledged that long clothes are hot in summer, but he said they are the best way to avoid bites. He also told us to see a doctor if I got a fever or if a bite became very large.

I followed every recommendation. Mia's mother bought me a pair of long pants, because I had not brought any. She also fixed the shorts I had ripped. The thick cream helped a lot, and after 4 days, most of the bites were gone. I should have listened to my cousin when she told me to wear long pants. If I had followed her suggestion, I would not have gotten so many bites.

Questions:
Where did Nora spend a week last July?
She spent a week with her cousin Mia, near a lake.
Why did Nora get so many bites?
She played between the bushes in the evening while she was wearing shorts.
What happened to Nora's shorts?
She ripped them on a bush.
What did Mr. Grant acknowledge?
He acknowledged that the bites looked bad, but he said they were not serious.
What was his first recommendation?
His first recommendation was a thick white cream for the bites.
What was his suggestion for the rest of her visit?
He suggested wearing long pants and long sleeves near the bushes in the evening.
What should Nora have done?
She should have listened to her cousin and worn long pants.

lessons.title: Back on the Field
lessons.summary: A retired baseball player hurts his hip, works hard in physical therapy and plays again.
lessons.text:
Frank Miller played baseball for his town's team for 25 years. When he was younger, he was one of the best athletes in the county. He could run faster than anyone on the team. After his retirement from his job at the bank, Frank finally had time for his favorite sport again. At 68, he joined a baseball league for players over 60. "In retirement, I get to be an athlete again," he liked to say.

Last spring, Frank fell while he was running to first base. He hurt his hip badly, and the doctor told him he needed physical therapy. "Your hip will heal," the doctor said, "but you have to work for it."

Frank started therapy 3 times a week with a therapist named Dana Cole. In the first weeks, the therapy was simple. Frank lay on a table, and Dana moved his leg slowly in different directions. Later, she gave him a resistance band, a long piece of rubber that makes exercise harder. Frank pulled the band with his leg again and again. "The resistance makes your muscles work," Dana explained. "Strong muscles protect your hip." Every week, she gave him a band with more resistance.

From the beginning, Frank had one intention: to play baseball again by the end of the summer. He told everyone about his intention. Dana told him it was possible, but only if he did his exercises at home every day. Frank never missed a single day.

In June, Frank walked around the park without pain for the first time. For him, it was a real achievement. "Walking without pain may sound small," he said, "but after an injury like this, it is a big achievement."

In August, Frank played his first game since he hurt his hip. Before the game, the league honored him for his 25 years in baseball. His wife and his grandchildren were there. "I am honored," Frank said to the players. "And I want to thank Dana. If she hadn't pushed me so hard, I would not be playing today."

Frank still does his exercises with the resistance band every morning. "Athletes my age have to take care of their bodies," he says. "I wish I had started these exercises years ago."

Questions:
What did Frank do after his retirement?
He joined a baseball league for players over 60.
How did Frank hurt his hip?
He fell while he was running to first base.
What does the resistance band do?
It makes exercise harder, so the muscles work.
What was Frank's intention?
His intention was to play baseball again by the end of the summer.
What was a real achievement for Frank?
Walking around the park without pain was a real achievement for him.
How did the league honor Frank?
The league honored him for his 25 years in baseball before his first game.

lessons.title: A Checkup for a Tiger
lessons.summary: An animal doctor at a wildlife park gives an old tiger her health check and also checks the wolves.
lessons.text:
Dr. Sara Quinn is an animal doctor at the Green Hills Wildlife Park. Her employer is the city, which owns the park. Today was a special day: Rosie, the park's oldest tiger, had her health check. Rosie gets a health check once a year.

Rosie's exact age is unknown. She was found as a young animal more than 15 years ago, and nobody knows the day she was born. "Her age is unknown, but she is old for a tiger," Dr. Quinn said. "Most tigers in the wild don't live this long."

To keep Rosie calm and safe, Dr. Quinn gave her medicine that made her sleep for an hour. Then the team got to work. They weighed the tiger, listened to her heart and looked at her eyes and teeth. Dr. Quinn also checked the tiger's tongue. A tiger's tongue is very rough, and it is covered with tiny hooks that help the animal clean its fur. "A healthy tongue should be pink and clean," Dr. Quinn explained, holding the tiger's tongue gently. Rosie's tongue was pink and clean. Her teeth were also in good condition for her age.

While the tiger was asleep, the maintenance team checked the fences around her area. Maintenance is a big part of life in the park: the maintenance team repairs fences, cleans pools and plants new trees. This year, the tiger's area got an upgrade. In the spring, the old pool was replaced with a bigger one, and the team added rocks where Rosie can lie in the sun. The upgrade was paid for by the city. "Our employer has been very good to us," Dr. Quinn said.

In the afternoon, Dr. Quinn visited the park's wolves. The park has a family of 6 wolves. One young wolf had a small cut on its leg. Dr. Quinn cleaned the cut, and the wolf ran back to the others.

The park's main goal is to preserve rare animals and to teach visitors about them. "Many tigers and wolves have lost their homes in the wild," Dr. Quinn said. "We want to help preserve these animals for our children and grandchildren."

By the end of the day, Rosie was awake and walking around her new pool. "If the health check had shown a problem, we would have treated it today," Dr. Quinn said. "But she is doing well. I hope she enjoys her upgrade."

Questions:
Who is Dr. Quinn's employer?
Her employer is the city, which owns the park.
Why is Rosie's exact age unknown?
She was found as a young animal, and nobody knows the day she was born.
What does a healthy tiger's tongue look like?
A healthy tongue should be pink and clean.
What does the maintenance team do?
It repairs fences, cleans pools and plants new trees.
What upgrade did the tiger's area get?
The old pool was replaced with a bigger one, and rocks were added.
What is the park's main goal?
Its main goal is to preserve rare animals and to teach visitors about them.

lessons.title: Is Chocolate Good for You?
lessons.summary: A short column looks calmly at chocolate, health and the way chocolate is sold.
lessons.text:
FOOD AND HEALTH: Is Chocolate Good for You?

I love chocolate, and I am not alone. In my office, people who don't eat chocolate are a small minority. When someone brings a box of chocolate to work, it is usually empty by lunch. So, is our favorite treat good for us or bad for us?

First, a few facts. Chocolate is made from the beans of the cacao tree, which grows in warm countries near the equator. Most of the world's beans come from West Africa. Ghana and Ivory Coast, 2 countries in this region, export more than half of the world's cacao beans. In some villages, a whole family runs a small enterprise that grows beans for export. In many cases, a small enterprise like this sells its beans to large companies, which turn them into chocolate in other countries.

Dark chocolate contains substances from the beans that may be good for the heart. Some studies have found that people who eat a little dark chocolate have slightly lower blood pressure. However, the outcome of a study depends on many things, and many of these studies were small. The outcome of one study is never the final answer.

There is also another side. Most chocolate bars contain a lot of sugar and fat. Milk chocolate contains fewer of the good substances than dark chocolate, and white chocolate contains almost none of them.

This is where advertising comes in. Some advertising presents chocolate as a healthy food. Don't let it fool you. A chocolate bar is a treat, not a medicine. Advertising for sweets has received a lot of criticism, especially advertising that is aimed at children. Because of this criticism, some countries have passed legislation that limits advertising for sweet foods on children's TV. Supporters of the legislation say it protects children, while some companies say parents should decide.

So, what is the answer? There is no absolute rule. Doctors do not say that chocolate is an absolute danger, and they do not say that it is a health food. My own rule is simple: a small piece of dark chocolate after lunch, and not the whole box. If I had followed this rule last week, I would not have eaten 6 pieces in one afternoon.

Questions:
Who are a small minority in the writer's office?
People who don't eat chocolate are a small minority.
Which 2 countries export more than half of the world's cacao beans?
Ghana and Ivory Coast export more than half of the beans.
Why is the outcome of one study never the final answer?
The outcome depends on many things, and many studies were small.
What does the writer say about advertising that presents chocolate as healthy?
The writer says not to let it fool you, because chocolate is a treat, not a medicine.
What have some countries done because of the criticism?
They have passed legislation that limits advertising for sweet foods on children's TV.
What is the writer's own rule?
A small piece of dark chocolate after lunch, and not the whole box.

lessons.title: Help in Every Language
lessons.summary: In an e-mail to volunteers, a woman who came to the US as an immigrant explains her translation work at a free health clinic.
lessons.text:
Subject: Welcome to our translation team

Dear new volunteers,

My name is Elena Torres, and I lead the translation team at the Hope Street Health Clinic. Before you start next week, I would like to write a short introduction to our work.

Our clinic is run by a small charity. The founder of the charity, Dr. Paul Adams, opened the clinic 12 years ago. He saw that many immigrants in our city did not visit a doctor, even when they were sick. Some of them could not pay, and many did not understand the forms or the doctor's instructions. Dr. Adams's answer was a free clinic with help in many languages. Today the charity has more than 50 volunteers, and our founder still sees patients every Monday.

I came to this country as an immigrant 15 years ago. Like many people who move here from overseas, I spoke very little English at first. I remember sitting in a doctor's office, holding a form I could not read. If a volunteer hadn't helped me with the translation, I would have left without seeing the doctor. That is why I joined this team.

Our team offers translation in 9 languages. Most of our patients come from overseas, and many of them have family overseas too. We translate forms, explain medicine labels and sit with patients during their visits. A good translation is clear and simple. It is better to use short sentences than difficult medical words.

There are 2 practical points. First, we have made an arrangement with City Hospital. Under this arrangement, our volunteers can go with patients to the hospital when they need tests. Please read the arrangement before your first visit there. Second, we have updated our patient forms. Please delete the old forms from your computers and use only the new ones, which you will find in our shared folder. If you have printed copies of the old forms, please throw them away too. It is easy to make a mistake with an old form, so please don't forget to delete them.

On Saturday at 10, there will be a short introduction for new volunteers at the clinic. You will meet Dr. Adams and the rest of the team. Thank you for giving your time to this charity. By the end of this year, our team will have helped more than 3,000 patients.

Best wishes,
Elena

Questions:
Who is the founder of the charity?
Dr. Paul Adams is the founder of the charity.
Why did Dr. Adams open the clinic?
He saw that many immigrants did not visit a doctor, even when they were sick.
Why did Elena join the translation team?
A volunteer helped her with a translation when she was a new immigrant.
What makes a good translation, according to Elena?
A good translation is clear and simple, with short sentences.
What arrangement has the clinic made with City Hospital?
Volunteers can go with patients to the hospital when they need tests.
What should volunteers do with the old forms?
They should delete the old forms and use only the new ones.
